Jess H: Heads-up — we need to decide behavior for Dedicated->Hosted routing when a region is saturated. Specifically: are we comfortable allowing Dedicated traffic to egress to Hosted as an overflow path for some customer tiers?
Samir: Quick context: today Dedicated traffic is strictly pinned. Spillover is blocked at the gateway to preserve isolation. Some customers have asked for optional overflow to avoid hard failures during infra incidents.
Maria T: We should separate two questions: (1) policy (which customers can overflow), (2) mechanics (how we route + billing + telemetry).
Ravi P: Strong NO unless we implement tenant-level opt-in and strict data-path guarantees. Don't want Dedicated customers surprised by data leaving their VPC.
Leo: From a product POV, customers care about uptime > absolute isolation sometimes. Could offer "best-effort overflow" as an opt-in toggle in Console with clear billing and audit logs.
Tia: Security note: even opt-in needs KMS/HSM compatibility; Hosted endpoints must inherit customer encryption keys or we must explicitly document key scope and consent.
DevOps Bot: policy-linter: dedicated-fallback requires explicit "tenant_consent" flag and audit_log.enabled = true — failing rule on current draft.
Samir: On mechanics: we need a deterministic routing decision in the gateway. Proposed fields on route_request: tier, region, tenant_consent, max_latency_slo_ms. Debate: should the router prefer model-variant compatibility (quantized variant) before choosing hosted cluster?
Jess H: Example decision tree I sketched: 
```
if dedicated.available && meets_slo(request):
  route -> dedicated
else if tenant_consent and hosted.compatible_variant and hosted.slo_warn < threshold:
  route -> hosted with metadata: origin=dedicated-overflow
else:
  fail -> soft 503 or degrade to smaller model
```
Samir: Two more constraints: quotas (don't let overflow bypass dedicated quotas) and billing (dedicated rate still applies or split billing?). I think split billing is cleaner: dedicated baseline + premium hosted egress units.
Maria T: Telemetry: need a new tag on traces: "overflow.path" and a dashboard showing overflow rate by tenant, model, region, time-of-day. Also add alerts: >1% overflow on a tenant for >5m triggers PagerDuty for account owner.
Ravi P: Also add a predicate: hosted must be the same compliance tier (e.g., SOC2 / EU data residency). If not, deny regardless of consent.
Leo: UX: Console toggle should show a modal: "Allow temporary routing to Redwood-hosted endpoints when Dedicated capacity is exhausted?" with checkboxes for billing consent and data residency confirmation. Add a one-click audit export.
Tia: Implementation detail: we must include an immutable event in customer audit stream whenever overflow happens: includes request_id, model_variant, target_cluster, reason_code, timestamp. Legal wants retention of that for 1 year for enterprise customers.
Samir: On internal API: we have two choices — extend route_policy_v1 with more fields, or introduce route_policy_v2 that explicitly models overflow sources. I prefer v2 to avoid breaking callers.
Jess H: Agree v2. Minimal fields: origin_hint, overflow_allowed:boolean, consent_token:string, allowed_destinations:list
DevOps Bot: ci/build: route-policy v2 schema tests: 12 passed, 2 failing (consent_token validation).
Maria T: Security review will need to run on route_policy_v2. Ravi/Tia, can you spearhead?
Ravi P: I can take it. Will draft a short RFC on data-path guarantees (keys, logs, residency).
Tia: I'll own the compliance checklist. Need to confirm HSM support on Hosted for each region.
Leo: Product action: add feature flag behind "overflow-optin" for next canary. We should also add a temporary acceptance criteria: visible billing preview + console audit export.
Jess H: Operational signals to implement now: queue_length per pool, tail latency, kv-cache hit-rate, overflow_count. We'll wire these to Console and to a per-tenant rollup view.
Samir: One more: fallback behavior for model variants. If dedicated has fp16-only variant but hosted serves an int8 variant, should we prefer model fidelity or latency? I vote for fidelity for paid tiers, latency for free tiers.
Maria T: Agree — expose policy tiers: strict_fidelity, cost_opt, latency_opt. Console shows what each tier means for outputs.
Ravi P: Implementation checklist I propose: 
- RFC: dedicated overflow policy (deadline: next Tue)
- route_policy_v2 schema + tests
- consent flow in Console + audit export
- telemetry: overflow metric + tenant dashboards
- security/compliance signoff
- canary rollout behind feature flag

Samir: I'll open the RFC and assign reviewers.
Leo: I'll mock the Console flow after RFC lands.
Jess H: Ok great. Next sync on Monday; action items in thread. :thumbsup:
DevOps Bot: deploy-bot: rolled out route-policy v2 schema changes to staging — please run integration tests.
Samir: @Ravi @Tia tagging you for security/compliance review.
Ravi P: On it.
Tia: Thanks.
Jess H: Closing for now — please add short comments here if you change scope.
